## Design

### 2026-11-06: After _a lot_ of trial and error, I decided on the layout of LEDs on the board. Each node in this graph represents an LED and a letter. The colour of a node represents the last element to reach that l

**2.5h**

After _a lot_ of trial and error, I decided on the layout of LEDs on the board. Each node in this graph represents an LED and a letter. The colour of a node represents the last element to reach that letter. The path from the root node to a letter is the elements needed in that order for the letter.

![Graph](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/WlipWVmF6UnTGNkVVXdowr37dB4xoM3o/e9abf928c972851950459076247452878b12318eff1d5354de3e6b090c902cbf.png)

As you can see, the nodes are in a grid, with vertical and horizontal edges connecting them. The root node is the middle and the nodes are horizontally symmetric around it. The root node will be controlled by a button below it.

The total number of LEDs is 28: 26 for the letters, 1 for the button indicator and 1 for the status indicator. The LEDs will all be RGB so I can make different colours have different meanings.

I did some research and reading to decide that I'll use WS2812Bs (package 5050) for the LEDs. They are 5mm x 5mm which is hopefully manageable for me to solder on, despite being SMDs.

The MCU chip I'll be using is the RP2040. I narrowed it down to either the Waveshare RP2040, the XIAO RP2040 v1.0, or the XIAO RP2040 Plus. After some consideration and learning about the differences in cost, size, and GPIOs, I decided on the XIAO RP2040 v1.0.

![RP2040](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/WlipWVmF6UnTGNkVVXdowr37dB4xoM3o/d9b15ee64176e814a5badd00be8059cea7c085c2067e0ea4e8a7127d8b456520.png)

I sourced the components needed and made a BOM, excluding the PCB:

![BOM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/WlipWVmF6UnTGNkVVXdowr37dB4xoM3o/ba723f8f1f90da598f1013eaee83f67c0440ec2b7a84ab59a41fc439f0a75048.png)

The goal is to have a very compact board, with the LEDs and one button on one side and the MCU and other buttons on the other side.

### 2026-11-08: I made some more changes to the layout and positioning of some components and graphics, and then added more silkscreen graphics too, notably, the big morse code message around the icosahedron wirefram

**4h**

I made some more changes to the layout and positioning of some components and graphics, and then added more silkscreen graphics too, notably, the big morse code message around the icosahedron wireframe on the back of the board. I'll leave it to you to figure out what that says. I'll just say, it took *a while* to arrange that properly and evenly and import it correctly on the board.

Here's what the board looked like after those changes:

![PCB](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/WlipWVmF6UnTGNkVVXdowr37dB4xoM3o/f3668d605fcdc6293cae28cacc715deb039913ac5e8b704d1fd0b5ab63c7dc73.png)

![Board front](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/WlipWVmF6UnTGNkVVXdowr37dB4xoM3o/0094ee35a3d3ba8b2f943b1eaf936ae4736c373104a6ed2f21bc92e19e5d01ed.png)

![Board back](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/WlipWVmF6UnTGNkVVXdowr37dB4xoM3o/360616f6d6498d8c36e2444d45562edc676a136052c1001cc517d573ecd27fb8.png)

Next I routed the board. I did the layout of the LEDs specifically based on the schematic so it would hopefully be easier to route, and that was definitely very helpful, though I still had to make some more changes. Most of the routing is on the F.Cu layer because all the LEDs are SMD and having it on the B.Cu layer means it would most likely cut through the decorative zone fill I added in the middle. I made that GND so it could act as a (pseudo) GND plane. Also, I tried really hard to minimize the number of vias and I think I succeeded in that.

![Routing](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/WlipWVmF6UnTGNkVVXdowr37dB4xoM3o/daf2977a89257898e7145ba8096b331eadc8ccedcf4996c9509b2cca01846e9f.png)

I'm not *very* happy with the routing because it looks very unorganized and also kinda messes with the neat appearance the front of the board had:

![Board front](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/WlipWVmF6UnTGNkVVXdowr37dB4xoM3o/cfeff9693e0605e7b6257cec50b14c69cb4bab9fbff85740fee693718d1d3f53.png)

Because of these reasons, I'll probably redo most of the routing before moving on.

### 2026-11-08: Last entry during design week!

**2.57h**

Last entry during design week!

First thing I did was reroute the PCB. Thankfully, this was much faster than expected and I'm pretty happy with the slight improvements I made. Here's the final routing:

![Routing](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/WlipWVmF6UnTGNkVVXdowr37dB4xoM3o/e1090cf0f78d05fcc5de822cb457baf3e1c2113c67e40dda224144ab60c1a2ce.png)

Next I finished the BOM and took all the cart screenshots.

![BOM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/WlipWVmF6UnTGNkVVXdowr37dB4xoM3o/59ca777dfa16b62a0f4f427d7f8f83f5edbe55296c2d842e98b76797620a25b7.png)

One thing to point out is that I only need 3 push buttons, but Robu requires each item in the cart to be at least ₹10, so I have to order at least 7.

Finally, I wrote out a detailed README for the project!
